svg.text: Go by the pin NAMES printed on the board. Everything is 3.3 V. Unplug the USB cable before you move a wire. Where two wires go to one pin, use the breadboard holes in that pin’s row.
chips facing up, antenna to the left, the two USB-C ports to the right
second wire: G pin → blue rail
the side with the TINY HOLE faces up; 6 pins
only these 5 pins; it shares SCL/SDA with the OLED
4-pin header on the top edge of the PCB
GPIO 2 → resistor → LONG leg (+). SHORT leg (−) → bottom blue rail.
1. Board in the breadboard + the three rail wires. Plug UART/COM into the Mac. Flash, watch the log.
2. OLED: 4 wires. The join code shows on the screen.
3. Mic: 6 wires. Press BOOT, talk, captions appear in the browser.
4. IMU: 5 wires. Slap the table and the device wakes.
5. LED: resistor + 2 wires. It lights while recording.
